strongest_angle: The popular concept of a structured 'Nine Realms' map is a modern invention, as ancient Norse sources provide contradictory, non-hierarchical descriptions of the cosmos.

key_facts.fact: The poem Völuspá mentions nine worlds existing within the tree Yggdrasill, but no surviving ancient text provides a definitive list or map of these locations.
Scholarly analysis by Eldar Heide shows that pre-Christian Scandinavian sources place the Æsir in multiple, conflicting locations including the east, west, sky, and under the sea.
The mythological tree Yggdrasill is described as the center of the cosmos, yet there is no evidence in source material that the realms were organized into vertical tiers or branches.
